info.title: Military Anthropometry API
info.description:
Body-measurement statistics of **military populations** for digital-human and mannequin tools (CATIA Human Builder, Siemens Jack,
RAMSIS, AutoCAD scripts, Unreal/Blender add-ons, spreadsheets) and for AI agents.

* **Populations** are *country × role* (Army, Air Force, Navy, Aircrew, Pilots, Recruits/trainees ...) and *sex* (`M`, `F`, `both`).
* **Design values** give P5, P50 and P95 (or any percentile from 0.1 to 99.9) of every measure, with sample size, reliability and sources.
* **Mannequin** gives one value per dimension at a single percentile: the dimension set for a boundary or reference manikin.
* Lengths are **millimetres**, body mass **kg**; every value carries its unit.
* The value endpoints (`/v1/design-values`, `/v1/mannequin`, `/v1/compare`) can also return **CSV** or **XML**: add `?format=csv` or `?format=xml`; `/v1/populations/{country}/{role}/{sex}`
  also takes a `.csv` / `.xml` / `.json` suffix on `sex`. `/v1/measures` has CSV too. CSV carries the data only; the notes travel in the `X-Disclaimer`, `X-Notes` and
  `X-Hidden-By-Reliability` response headers, and XML has a `<notes>` element.
* In URL **paths** use ids (`united-states`, `recruits-trainees`) or names; names that contain `/` (Recruits/trainees) work too. The query-string forms take names or ids.
* List parameters are comma separated: `measures=stature,mass,sitting_height`.

**Reliability.** `min_reliability` defaults to `medium` (high and medium). `high` keeps only values whose sources are raw data, validated
tables or official defence documents, with printed percentiles and at least 100 people. `low` (or `all`) includes everything.

**Percentiles.** P5, P50 and P95 are the roll-up values (see `percentile_basis`: `reported` by the one survey, `pooled` from several surveys, or `estimated` from mean and SD).
Other percentiles are interpolated or extrapolated from them. Each dimension is the requested percentile *of that dimension alone*: a set
of same-percentile dimensions is a boundary case, not a typical body.

**Surveys.** By default the values combine every survey of the population, as the website does, which can mix decades (see `n_surveys`, `survey_spread_pct` and the notes).
Pass `survey=latest` for the most recent well-covered survey, or an id from `/v1/populations/{country}/{role}/surveys`.

get.summary: Version, counts, units, reliability and percentile definitions, attribution

get.description: Measures with data, filtered by words in the name (`q`; whole words and common synonyms such as weight = mass, width = breadth), category, and optionally by population. Best matches first: harmonized measures before as-published ones. `X-Total-Count` gives the number of matches before `limit`.

get.summary: One measure and the populations that have it
Design values of one population (P5, P50, P95 or any percentiles)
get.description: The same path works on the static copy of the data: `/api/v1/populations/{country}/{role}/{sex}.json` (or `.csv`), with all reliability levels and the default percentiles 5, 50, 95. `sex` may end in `.json`, `.csv` or `.xml`. `country` and `role` take ids or names (`united-states`, `recruits-trainees` or `Recruits/trainees`).

get.summary: Titles, links and official documents of a source id

survey.title: Survey
survey.description: `latest` when each population's most recent survey was used; null for the combined values.

no_data.title: No Data
no_data.description: Requested countries or roles that have no result, under the keys `countries` and `roles`.

years.title: Years
years.description: First and last year of measurement of the surveys behind this value.

available.title: Available
available.description: Valid values to choose from, or (when `closest` is true) only the nearest matches.

closest.title: Closest
closest.description: True when `available` holds the nearest matches to what was asked, not every valid value.

core.title: Core
core.description: Stature (mm), body mass (kg) and sitting height (mm) at this percentile, when available.

values.title: Values
values.description: Measure key to value in the measure's unit (see `units`): the flat dimension set.

units.title: Units
units.description: Measure key to unit for every key in `values`: millimetres for lengths, but also kg, kg/m2, years, %, N, ratios ...

caution.title: Caution
caution.description: Keys of `values` that need care, with the reasons: lower reliability, estimated or extrapolated, surveys that disagree.

unavailable.title: Unavailable
unavailable.description: Measures that exist for this population but have only a mean (no percentiles), so they are not in `values`.

populations.title: Populations
populations.description: Number of country/role populations with data.

harmonized.title: Harmonized
harmonized.description: True for the 59 measures defined the same way in every survey; false for as-published measures, whose definition is whatever the source printed.

unit.title: Unit
unit.description: mm, kg, kg/m2, years, or the printed unit of an as-published measure (%, ratio, degrees ...).

percentiles.title: Percentiles
percentiles.description: Value at each requested percentile, keyed "p5", "p50", "p95", "p97.5" ...

percentile_basis.title: Percentile Basis
percentile_basis.description: How each percentile was obtained: `reported` by the one survey it comes from, `pooled` from several surveys that each printed theirs (no source prints this exact number), `estimated` from mean and SD, `interpolated` or `extrapolated` from P5/P50/P95.

reliability_note.title: Reliability Note
reliability_note.description: Why the value is not high reliability.

n_surveys.title: N Surveys
n_surveys.description: Number of surveys combined in this value (1 = a single survey).

survey_spread_pct.title: Survey Spread Pct
survey_spread_pct.description: When several surveys are combined: (largest survey mean - smallest) / combined mean, in percent. Large values mean the surveys disagree (different landmark definitions, or real change in body size over the years).

official_documents.title: Official Documents
official_documents.description: Official defence or standards documents the data come from, if any.

sources.title: Sources
sources.description: Source ids; GET /v1/sources/{id} gives titles and links.

printed_name.title: Printed Name
printed_name.description: The name the source printed, when it differs from the common name.

role.title: Role
role.description: Survey population: Army, Air Force, Navy, Aircrew, Pilots, Recruits/trainees ...

sex.title: Sex
sex.description: M, F, or both (mixed or not stated).

survey.description: Set when one survey was requested; null for the combined values of the population.

surveys_combined.title: Surveys Combined
surveys_combined.description: Surveys that make up the combined values (empty when a single survey was requested).

years.title: Years
years.description: First and last year of measurement.

surveys_in_combined_values.title: Surveys In Combined Values
surveys_in_combined_values.description: Of those, the surveys that contribute to the combined values.

APIKeyHeader.description: Needed only when the server sets ANTHRO_API_KEYS.
APIKeyHeader.name: X-API-Key
